items.title: What does turbo replacement cost in the UK?
items.description: The short answer: Turbo replacement costs range from £450 to £3,000+ depending on single vs twin turbo, vehicle make, and parts quality. Small cars typically cost £450-£1,500 , family cars £800-£2,500 , and premium/performance vehicles £1,500-£3,500+ . Repair services start from £195+VAT , exchange remanufactured units from £495+VAT , and new turbos from £1,000+ . The longer answer: For most UK drivers, turbo failure is a common and expensive issue. Here's what you can expect:

items.title: 10 questions to ask before replacing your turbo

cards.title: 1. "What's included in the replacement price?"
cards.text: Get a full written breakdown. Ask about: turbo unit, gaskets, seals, oil and filter change, oil lines, and labour.
cards.fullText: 1. "What's included in the replacement price?" Get a full written breakdown. Ask about: turbo unit, gaskets, seals, oil and filter change, oil lines, and labour.

cards.title: 2. "Is this a repair, exchange, or new turbo?"
cards.text: Understand what you're paying for. Repair is cheapest but may not be possible. Exchange is best value. New is most expensive.
cards.fullText: 2. "Is this a repair, exchange, or new turbo?" Understand what you're paying for. Repair is cheapest but may not be possible. Exchange is best value. New is most expensive.

cards.title: 3. "What warranty do you offer on the replacement?"
cards.text: Typical warranty: repair 6-12 months, exchange 12-24 months, new 12-24 months. Get it in writing.
cards.fullText: 3. "What warranty do you offer on the replacement?" Typical warranty: repair 6-12 months, exchange 12-24 months, new 12-24 months. Get it in writing.

cards.title: 4. "Will you flush the oil system?"
cards.text: When a turbo fails, it sends debris into the oil system. The oil system should be flushed before the new turbo is fitted.
cards.fullText: 4. "Will you flush the oil system?" When a turbo fails, it sends debris into the oil system. The oil system should be flushed before the new turbo is fitted.

cards.title: 5. "Will you replace the oil feed and return lines?"
cards.text: These lines can be blocked with debris. Many specialists recommend replacing them to prevent premature failure.
cards.fullText: 5. "Will you replace the oil feed and return lines?" These lines can be blocked with debris. Many specialists recommend replacing them to prevent premature failure.

cards.title: 6. "What's the timeline from booking to completion?"
cards.text: Small car turbo replacement typically takes 1-2 days. Twin turbo/SUV takes 2-4 days.
cards.fullText: 6. "What's the timeline from booking to completion?" Small car turbo replacement typically takes 1-2 days. Twin turbo/SUV takes 2-4 days.

cards.title: 7. "Is the intercooler contaminated?"
cards.text: If the turbo has failed, the intercooler may be contaminated with oil. It may need cleaning or replacement.
cards.fullText: 7. "Is the intercooler contaminated?" If the turbo has failed, the intercooler may be contaminated with oil. It may need cleaning or replacement.

cards.title: 8. "Do you have experience with my vehicle/engine type?"

cards.fullText: 8. "Do you have experience with my vehicle/engine type?" Some turbos require specialist knowledge. Ask about their experience with your specific vehicle.

cards.title: 9. "What's the labour cost and how many hours?"
cards.text: Get a clear breakdown of labour hours and rates. This should be part of the written quote.
cards.fullText: 9. "What's the labour cost and how many hours?" Get a clear breakdown of labour hours and rates. This should be part of the written quote.

faqs.answer: If the turbo has minor wear (worn bearings, seal leak), repair is viable and cheaper. If the turbo has seized or has significant damage, exchange or new replacement is the only option. A specialist will inspect and advise.

faqs.question: Can I replace a turbo myself? +
faqs.answer: Turbo replacement is not a DIY job for most owners. It requires specialist tools, knowledge of the turbo system, and careful handling to prevent damage. Incorrect installation can cause premature failure. Use a specialist.

faqs.question: How long does a turbo last? +
faqs.answer: A turbo should last 100,000-150,000 miles with regular oil changes and proper maintenance. However, some turbos fail earlier due to design issues (common on some engines) or poor maintenance (infrequent oil changes).

faqs.question: Does turbo replacement affect insurance? +
faqs.answer: Yes - any major mechanical work, including turbo replacement, should be declared to your insurer . The work may affect vehicle value and should be recorded.

mainEntity.name: How much does turbo replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turbo replacement costs range from £450 to £3,000+ depending on single vs twin turbo, vehicle make, and parts quality. Small cars cost £450-£1,500, family cars £800-£2,500, and premium/performance vehicles £1,500-£3,500+. Repair from £195+VAT, exchange from £495+VAT, new from £1,000+.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loss of power, excessive smoke (blue/white), whistling or siren noise, engine management light, oil burning smell, grinding noise, and boost pressure errors. Whistling and loss of power are the most common early signs.

mainEntity.name: Can I drive with a failing turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: No - stop driving as soon as possible. A failing turbo can send metal debris into the oil system, damaging the engine. If the turbo seizes completely, it can cause catastrophic engine failure (£4,000+ to replace).

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between turbo repair, exchange, and new?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair: Turbo stripped and worn parts replaced (£195-£600). Exchange: Your old turbo exchanged for a remanufactured unit (£495-£1,500+). New: Brand new turbo from OEM or aftermarket (£500-£3,000+). Exchange is the most popular option.

mainEntity.name: How long does turbo replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typical replacement time is 1-4 days. Small car turbos take 3-5 hours (1-2 days). Twin turbo and SUV turbos take 8-20 hours (2-4 days).

mainEntity.name: Does turbo replacement require an oil change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - absolutely essential. When a turbo fails, it sends metal debris into the oil system. The oil and filter must be changed to prevent debris from damaging the new turbo or engine bearings.

mainEntity.name: Should I replace oil lines when replacing a turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - strongly recommended. The oil feed and return lines can be blocked with debris. If not replaced or cleaned, the new turbo may be starved of oil and fail prematurely.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I ignore a failing turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: The turbo will eventually fail completely. Metal debris enters the oil system, damaging engine bearings, camshafts, and other components. Engine replacement costs £4,000+. Early replacement is much cheaper.

mainEntity.name: Why does turbo replacement cost more on some vehicles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turbo location affects labour time. Front-mounted turbos are accessible (3-5 hours). Rear-mounted turbos require significant disassembly (8-15 hours). Twin turbos cost double the parts cost and more labour.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common turbo failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common failure is worn bearings - caused by oil starvation, debris in the oil, or age. Actuator failure is also common, especially on VAG (VW/Audi) vehicles.
